gradient_objective: Fit incident_full pooled valid-cell standardized MAE, evaluated with fixed weights. Save derivatives of each disjoint regional error SUM with respect to per-sample per-node direct injection strengths. Divide all regions by the same whole-fit valid-cell count to obtain contributions to the full loss; also report each region's own mean derivative. Sum coordinates for the shared scalar derivative. At g=1, v12c scalar-logit derivative is one half of the direct-strength derivative.
gradient_interpretation: Input-coordinate derivatives, not MLP parameter gradients. Region-vector cosine and cancellation do not prove optimizer conflict in a shared neural gate. Positive derivative favors a local decrease in strength. At g=1 the identity penalty derivative is zero. No inference about penalty dominance at trained weights. No optimizer or parameter updates.
identity: g=1 must exactly reproduce native full predictions on every evaluated batch. g=0 removes only ICSF injection; LayerNorm, original TIID context and all downstream computations remain. g=2 is a diagnostic endpoint, not a finite-logit value of the v12c sigmoid gate.
limitations: Reuse v12c time eligibility, original A and original all-train scaler; development data already inspected.
Hash entire frozen train artifacts for identity; dataset wrappers may load train metadata/context but only fit/selection samples are fetched for evaluation.
Full-period pooled gradient is not the sequence of equally stepped minibatch gradients used by Adam.
MAE and graph computations can be nonsmooth; finite strength differences need not match infinitesimal derivatives.
Finite grid cannot establish an optimum or exclude all useful state-dependent gates.
No confidence intervals, new thresholds, learning-rate search, model selection or test authorization.
